question: A confidence interval to estimate the population mean will be more precise when:

options.opb: The greater the dispersion of the sample.
options.opd: The greater the level of trust.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lower confidence level" -> "wider confidence interval" -> "less precision in estimating population mean" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Greater dispersion of the sample" -> "increased variability" -> "wider confidence interval" -> "less precision in estimating population mean" -> 40%
CHAIN: "Smaller sample size" -> "greater sampling error" -> "wider confidence interval" -> "less precision in estimating population mean" -> 35%
CHAIN: "Greater level of trust" -> "not directly related to statistical precision" -> "unclear impact on confidence interval" -> 50%
analysis: A confidence interval becomes more precise with a lower confidence level because it results in a narrower interval. Higher confidence levels increase the width of the interval, making it less precise. Greater dispersion in the sample and smaller sample sizes lead to wider intervals, while greater trust does not directly affect precision.
